sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
அநாத ரக்ஷகி அபீதகுசாம்பிகே விநாயக ஜனனீ
மகேசன் மனோகரி மதுசூதனன் சோதரி
sections.translit:
anAdha rakshaki apIthakuchAmbikE vinAyaka jananI
magesan manOgari madhusUdhanan sOdhari
sections.en: Goddess Apeethakuchambal, you are the protector of orphans, mother of Ganesha, darling consort of Siva, and sister of Vishnu.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
தரித்ர ஹாரிணி வேதாகம காரிணி மூலோக பாலினி
சுசரித்ர ராகவாசினி சூலதாரிணி சுபதாயினி
sections.translit:
dharidhra hAriNi vEdhAgama kAriNi mUlOka pAlini
sucharithra rAgavAsini sUladhAriNi subhadhAyini
sections.en: You are the destroyer of abject poverty, the source and cause of the scriptures and rituals, protector of the three universes. You dwell in the melody of Sucharitra raga, carry the trident and bestow auspiciousness all around.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
போத நாயகியே தேனருவியெனச் செவிகுளிரும்
நாத ஸ்வரூபமே வரையறை செய்து உணர்ந்து
ஓத இயலா ஓங்கார உட்பொருளே உமையே
காத தூரம் என்றெண்ணாமல் எளியனை வந்தாதரி (சங்கரி)
sections.translit:
bOdha nAyakiyE thEnaruviyenach chevikuLirum
nAdha swarUpamE varaiyaRai seydhu uNarndhu
Odha iyalA OngkAra utporuLE umaiyE
kAdha dhUram endReNNAmal eLiyanai vandhAdhari (sankari)
sections.en: You are the source of all teachings. You embody a sound that flows like nectar from a fountain. You are the essence of the primordial voice, boundless and beyond what can be measured or learned. Goddess Uma, please save this poor soul from his longing. Do not calculate the distance or be dissuaded by how far away I am.

notes: Arunachaleshwara temple in Thiruvannamalai has a shrine for Devi as Apeethakuchambal or Unnamulai Amman both words (Sanskrit and Tamil) meaning Ambal’s breast milk had never been consumed by babies. The implication is that she did not breastfeed Ganesha or Muruga. However, Devi does feed the milk of divine knowledge to her devotees. She became one with Siva and the Lord assumed the name Ardhanariswara. There is a detailed prayer of Ambal by Appayya Dikshitar who pays high compliments to the calmness of Devi who is an integral part of the eternal flame, Lord Siva. The blog below also provides the meaning of the deity’s name. It is interesting that the Sanskrit and Tamil names of the deity mean the same thing. Details can be found in the following links: Apeethakuchambal aka Unnamulai Amman of Thiruvannamalai Appayya Dikshitar’s Prayer to Apeethakuchamba
